judge_assessment.explanation: The first hard failure is confirmed and is decisive on its own. final_response.md contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'pdf' in any case, and names no filename: it opens 'Three documents, all compiled and gated: a 10-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide.' scripts/score_eval_run.py's response_surfaces() returns True only if the response contains the artifact's filename, or contains '.pdf'/'pdfs' together with a role phrase; with no 'pdf' token anywhere, all three roles fail and the machine gate raises artifact_not_surfaced three times. So the judge's critical observation that 'the machine gate independently flags all three requested artifacts as not surfaced' is correct, even though the packet's machine_observation JSON does not itself carry that field. Every other case in my batch says 'Three PDFs' or names ws_*.pdf explicitly; this one says 'documents'. The second hard failure is wrong on its facts. Problems 3, 5, 7 and 9 do not require any construction. The sheet's directions say so in terms: 'The coordinate check problems do not ask you to construct anything. They hand you the output of a construction and ask you to test the property that construction is supposed to guarantee.' Problem 3 hands the student P(-1,8) and asks for PA and PB; problem 5 hands two hexagon vertices and asks for the distance between them; problem 7 hands A, B, C, D and asks for AB and CD; problem 9 hands the circumcentre O(4,3) and asks for OA, OB and OC. A distance check is exactly the right machine check for each. What IS uncovered on those four problems is the prose slot the judge did not name: each opens 'Name the property...' / 'State the claim...' / 'State what the intersection ... is guaranteed to be', and none of those has an entry. That is a real gap of the same family as the rest of the shard, but it is not the gap the judge described, and 'four open geometric constructions are falsely represented by coordinate-distance checks' misstates what the artifact does. All eight distances recompute: PA = PB = 5*sqrt(2) = 7.07; hexagon side 10.00; AB = CD = 10; OA = OB = OC = 5 (the circumcentre of the right triangle at the hypotenuse midpoint). REJECT stands on the surfacing failure.

strengths_to_preserve: The three-facet decomposition is the right analysis of what constructions actually demand, and the sheet is built on it: plan-the-construction (1, 2, 6), justify-the-construction (4, 8, 10), check-on-coordinates (3, 5, 7, 9). Most construction worksheets collapse all three into 'do the construction'; separating them makes each one gradeable.

The coordinate-check design is the sheet's real invention, and the answer key names it: 'The four coordinate problems are the antidote: they hand back the output of a construction and ask the student to test the very property the construction promised.' It converts an ungradeable compass drawing into a checkable claim without pretending the drawing itself was checked -- and the six genuinely open items stay honestly manual.

The directions define what counts as a plan step with real precision: 'Each step must say where the compass point sits, whether the opening changes, and what gets drawn. "Draw an arc" is not a step until it says centred where and with what radius.' The key's grading note then names the recurring failure it is designed to catch: 'a plan whose arcs have no stated centre or radius, and a justification that appeals to the picture instead of to equal radii'.

Problem 10(c) is a genuinely hard and correct challenge: a classmate claims repeated bisection also trisects a segment, and the student must explain why it cannot. Powers of two never reach thirds, and asking that question is what distinguishes a student who has memorised the bisection procedure from one who understands what it produces.

Multi-entry ids are used correctly for the numeric work -- id 3 carries two distance entries (PA and PB), id 7 two (AB and CD), id 9 three (OA, OB, OC) -- so each equality the property claims is independently checked rather than asserted from one computation.

root_causes.description: The final delivery response describes the three artifacts in prose ('Three documents ... a 10-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide') and never names a file. SKILL.md step 6 says to 'report the three output paths clearly', but nothing verifies that the delivery message did so, and build.sh's gate summary prints the three PDF paths to the LOG rather than into the response. So a build can end green with every artifact on disk and none of them reachable by the reader.
evidence: final_response.md: zero occurrences of 'pdf' (case-insensitive); no filename anywhere in the file
scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces(): requires the artifact filename, or '.pdf'/'pdfs' plus a role phrase
gate_log.txt prints the three built PDF paths under a '-- PDFs --' heading, into the log only
the other nine cases in my batch all write 'Three PDFs' or name ws_*.pdf / ak_*.pdf / ss_*.pdf explicitly

root_causes.description: The four coordinate-check problems each open with a required prose claim -- name the property, state the claim, state what the intersection is guaranteed to be -- before the computation. Per-id coverage is satisfied by the distance entries, so those claims are recorded nowhere. This is the shard's dominant defect, in a mild form: the numeric half is verified thoroughly (two or three distances per problem) and the named property is not.
evidence: worksheet problem 3: 'Name the property a perpendicular bisector guarantees about P, then test it'

worksheet problem 5: 'State the claim that construction depends on, then test it'; problem 7: 'Name the property the copy construction guarantees'; problem 9: 'State what the intersection of two perpendicular bisectors is guaranteed to be'
worksheet directions: 'Say which property you are testing before you compute'
verify.json ids 3, 5, 7, 9: distance entries only, no manual companion

improvements.title: The delivery response names no PDF and no filename for any of the three artifacts
improvements.proposed_change: Make the delivery step mechanical instead of remembered. Have scripts/build.sh emit a ready-to-paste delivery block at the end of a green run -- one line per artifact with its role and its full path (ws_*.pdf, ak_*.pdf, ss_*.pdf) -- and have SKILL.md step 6 instruct that this block be reproduced in the response rather than paraphrased. Add a check that fails the run when the response file that accompanies a build does not contain all three filenames: the predicate already exists as response_surfaces() in scripts/score_eval_run.py, so lift it into a shared helper and call it from both the scorer and the build so the author sees the failure before delivery instead of at judging.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture case whose final_response.md reads 'Three documents: the worksheet, the answer key and the study guide' with all three PDFs present on disk; assert the surfacing check reports artifact_not_surfaced for all three roles. It already does so in the scorer; the regression is that the same predicate must now fail the BUILD, which it does not today.
improvements.expected_impact: Eliminates an entire hard-failure category that is unrelated to the mathematics: the artifacts here are complete, correct and gated, and the run is rejected because the message describing them says 'documents' instead of naming three files. This is the cheapest hard failure in the suite to remove.
improvements.risk: Low. It adds output to a green build and one predicate call; the only care needed is that a legitimate delivery channel that attaches files rather than naming paths must still pass, so the check should accept either an attachment manifest or the filenames.

improvements.title: The named property each coordinate check tests is required and unrecorded
improvements.proposed_change: Require a companion `manual` entry wherever an item asks for a named claim alongside a computation, with the expected claim in `desc`. Enforce it in scripts/verify.py by scanning the directions block and each problem segment for naming imperatives ('name the property', 'state the claim', 'state what ... is guaranteed to be', 'say which property') and exiting 2 listing every id with no manual entry. On curr-350 that fires on ids 3, 5, 7 and 9 -- the four problems where the sheet verifies the arithmetic thoroughly and leaves the claim being tested unrecorded.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem reading 'Name the property a perpendicular bisector guarantees about P, then test it: compute PA and PB' with two distance entries and no manual entry; assert verify.py exits 2 naming the id. It exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: Completes an already-good design. The coordinate-check idea is sound precisely because the property is the point and the distances are the test; recording the distances and not the property inverts that emphasis in the verification data.
improvements.risk: Low-to-medium. A directions-level scan flags all four ids at once; exit 2 keeps the cost to a line of author review.

improvements.title: The key describes constructions in prose without showing a completed compass-and-straightedge figure
improvements.proposed_change: For each of the six manual construction and justification items, add a rendered figure of the finished construction to the answer key -- the arcs, their centres, and the labelled intersection points (M and N on the perpendicular bisector, R on the angle bisector, C on the equilateral triangle) -- so a marker can compare a student's drawing against a picture rather than against a paragraph. scripts/render_figures.py already generates to-scale figures from JSON in other cases in this run; extend its figure kinds with an arcs-and-intersections form so the key's figure is generated from the same declared data as its prose.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_figures.py declaring a perpendicular-bisector construction figure (segment AB, two arc centres, two intersections M and N) and assert the renderer emits arcs centred at A and B and labels both intersections. No such figure kind exists today.
improvements.expected_impact: Addresses the one dimension the judge scored below the others (answer_key_quality 3). On a constructions sheet, a marker grading a drawing against prose is doing the harder half of the work unaided.
improvements.risk: Medium. New figure kinds are the most common source of layout regressions; the seven-page worksheet is already at its page budget, so the figures must go in the key only, and the compile-ak page budget must be rechecked.

case_summary: The construction reasoning is strong and the sheet's central idea is genuinely good: it splits constructions into planning, justifying and checking, and the four coordinate-check problems hand back a construction's output so the property it promised becomes testable without pretending a compass drawing was machine-checked. Six items are honestly manual with substantive descs, the numeric halves are thoroughly covered (two distances on problem 3, two on 7, three on 9), and all eight recompute -- 7.07 twice, 10.00, 10 twice, 5 three times. The run fails for a reason unrelated to the mathematics: final_response.md contains no filename and not one occurrence of the string 'pdf', so score_eval_run.py's response_surfaces() predicate fails for all three roles and the artifacts are never delivered. I disagree with the judge's second hard failure. Problems 3, 5, 7 and 9 require no construction at all -- the directions state 'The coordinate check problems do not ask you to construct anything' -- so calling their distance checks a false representation of open constructions misdescribes the artifact. The genuine gap on those four is the prose slot the judge did not name: each asks the student to name the property being tested, and no entry records it.
